summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for elective coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) due to severe two-vessel coronary disease and worsening dyspnea on exertion. She underwent a successful triple bypass using the left internal mammary artery and saphenous vein grafts. Postoperatively, she was managed in the CVICU, extubated on postoperative day 2, and transitioned to the telemetry floor by day 6. She developed acute kidney injury with rising creatinine from 1.5 to 3.1, prompting nephrology consultation and discontinuation of diuretics. A urinary tract infection caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa was identified and treated with ciprofloxacin. Her wounds healed well, and she was discharged on postoperative day 8 to extended care rehabilitation with plans for close outpatient follow-up, including twice-weekly renal labs. Medications were adjusted for safety, including switching from nebivolol to metoprolol and continuing clopidogrel instead of aspirin due to allergy.
